cards.title: Testify
cards.why: The DC Council holds public hearings, and its committees accept testimony from members of the public — young people included. Public witnesses get a few minutes each. That is a real Audience with real power, on a published calendar, and almost no chapter has ever used it. The One-Page Ask is what you bring.

parts.heading: The One-Page Ask
parts.body: Six parts, in order, one page.
items: The problem, in two sentences.
The DC-specific data point — a ward disparity from named DC Health data, a pathway gap, a funding line. Cited and dated.
The single ask, stated as a verb a named person can perform. Not ‘support health education’. ‘Fund the health science pathway at two more high schools in the FY28 budget.’
Who that person is — the committee, the councilmember, the agency.
The date by which it must happen, and why that date.
What happens next if the answer is no.

parts.heading: At the hearing
items: Check the hearing notice for the witness time limit and the sign-up method. Follow both exactly.
Read the One-Page Ask aloud. It fits. Submit the written version for the record.
Say who you represent, and what you are and are not authorised to commit. See Speak for the Affiliate.
Say ‘I am excited’ in the corridor first.

parts.heading: Afterwards
parts.body: Report back to the chapter and the SEC — what was said, what the committee asked, what happens next. That closes the Influence box.

steps: Draft the six parts. Have someone score the ask line: could a named person do this on Monday?
Find the next relevant hearing on the Council calendar. Sign up as a public witness.
Rehearse it as Rung 4 of the Speaking Ladder — timed, scored on the one criterion: the ask is in the first thirty seconds.
cards.where: Council hearings on health, education, or the budget. The same document, shortened, is the Internal Advocacy Pack an advisor takes to a principal.
cards.coach: The first testimony is the hard one. Go with them. Sit behind them in the hearing room, say nothing, and debrief within 24 hours using the three questions. The second one they do alone.

grounding.model: Structured policy ask; DC Council public hearing process
grounding.citation: The One-Page Ask is a DC HOSA construction built on the Lundy Model (R). DC Council hearing procedures — witness sign-up, time limits, written testimony — are as published in each committee’s hearing notice; confirm per hearing.
grounding.caveat: Hearing procedures and time limits vary by committee and are set in each notice. Never rely on a remembered limit.

cards.title: Speak for the Affiliate
cards.why: The moment a state officer is introduced to a hospital partner or a Council staffer, they need to know where their authority ends. Right now they learn it by getting it wrong. This card is written as permissions rather than prohibitions, so it enables rather than chills.

parts.heading: You may, on your own authority
items: Describe DC HOSA, its mission, its pillars, and its programmes accurately.
Share published figures — dated, from the membership report — and say when you do not know one.
Accept a speaking invitation for yourself, and say you will confirm the affiliate’s participation.
Take a partner’s interest back to the SEC and the State Advisor, with a date by which they will hear.
Give your own view, labelled as your own.

parts.heading: You may not, without the State Advisor
items: Agree a partnership, sponsorship, or any arrangement with money or the DC HOSA name in it.
Quote a figure you have not seen published — membership, chapters, budget.
Respond to media on behalf of the affiliate.
Sign anything.
Commit a chapter to anything. Chapters commit themselves.

parts.heading: The sentence that handles every edge case
parts.body: ‘That is a great question and it is not mine to answer — I will take it to the State Advisor and you will hear back by [date].’ Said with confidence, it reads as competence, not as weakness.

steps: Read both lists at SEC orientation. Every officer.
Write the edge-case sentence on the back of your name badge, literally.
The first time you use it, tell the State Advisor the same day.
cards.where: Every partner meeting, hearing, media contact, and conference. It is the second half of the Voting Delegate card — a delegate votes as a representative, not an individual, and needs the same boundary.
cards.coach: This gap is real and the affiliate has been closing it case by case. Write the two lists into SEC orientation and the Portfolio Charter so nobody learns them the hard way. And when an officer uses the edge-case sentence correctly, tell them — that is the behaviour you want repeated.

grounding.model: Representation and delegated authority — governance convention
grounding.citation: DC HOSA governance construction, consistent with the Bylaws’ allocation of authority to the State Advisor. Practitioner convention; not a research finding.
